newsitem.title: LEBANON: Most bank shares rise in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: Most bank shares rise in Beirut.

text.p: Two of the three bank shares on the Beirut Stock Exchange rose in heavy demand on Wednesday and the rest of the shares on the market were unchanged.
Newcomer Bank of Beirut rose to $3.375 from $3.25, bringing its spectacular rise since its April 11 debut to 55 percent over issue price.
Demand for BOB remained high at 2,543,875 but was about half Tuesday's 5,400,256. Supply was 111,374 shares, all of which were sold.
Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce rose to $15.125 from $15 while Banque Audi was unchanged at $20.
Both shares were in heavy demand. Demand for BLC totalled 59,760 against a supply of 12,000 while demand for Audi was 72,337 shares against 25,185.
BLC and Banque Audi have jumped 34 percent and 33 percent respectively since they made their debuts on December 30 and January 20.
A block of 41,264 BOB shares traded on the floor at $3.4375. Another block of 9,500 shares traded on the floor at $3.375.
The LIBX bank index rose 1.55 percent to 131.10. The BLOM general index rose 0.04 percent to 913.57 and the LISPI rose 0.75 percent to 86.86.

Solidere A and B shares were unchanged at $10.25 and $10.75 respectively. Ciments Libanais, the only stock traded out of the other four listed companies, was unchanged at $1.2812 on turnover of 44,500 shares.
Total market turnover was 340,813 shares compared with 389,374 shares on Tuesday. Value fell to $2,290,210 from $3,083,737.
There was no trade in Ciments Blancs, Eternit and Uniceramic.
